questions.scenario: A nightly job loads a 3 GB card-scheme settlement file with `Files.readAllLines(path)` and the container is OOMKilled.
questions.question: What is the right way to process the file?
options: Stream it line by line with Files.lines (closed with try-with-resources) or a BufferedReader
questions.explanation: readAllLines holds every line in memory. Streaming reads one line at a time in constant memory; the stream must be closed to release the file handle.

questions.scenario: An API takes a file name and serves `inbox.resolve(name)`. A tester requests `../../etc/passwd` and gets the file.
questions.question: What check prevents this?
options: Normalise the resolved path and verify it still startsWith the inbox directory
questions.explanation: resolve followed by normalize removes ../ segments; if the result isn't under the allowed directory, reject it. This is the standard path-traversal defence.

questions.scenario: Customer names with accents and the ₦ symbol appear garbled in an exported CSV opened by a partner.
questions.question: What is the most likely cause and fix?
options: Bytes were written or read with a different charset; specify the charset explicitly (e.g. StandardCharsets.UTF_8) on both sides and agree it with the partner
Use a byte stream instead of a writer
questions.explanation: Text becomes bytes through a charset. Mismatched charsets garble non-ASCII characters; naming the charset in code and in the interface contract fixes it.

questions.scenario: Another system polls an outbox folder and sometimes picks up half-written statement files.
questions.question: Which pattern stops that?
options: Write to a temporary file in the same file system, then Files.move it into the outbox with ATOMIC_MOVE
Make the file read-only after writing
questions.explanation: An atomic rename makes the complete file appear at once; readers never see a partial file.

questions.scenario: A `Session` class implements Serializable and has `private transient String accessToken`. After deserialisation the token is null.
questions.question: Why?
options: transient fields are not serialised and come back with their default value (null)
questions.explanation: transient excludes a field from the serial form, which is exactly right for secrets such as tokens.

questions.scenario: A team adds a field to a Serializable class that has no explicit serialVersionUID. Reading previously saved data now throws InvalidClassException.
questions.question: What prevents this in future?
options: Declare a private static final long serialVersionUID (annotated @Serial) and manage compatible changes deliberately
questions.explanation: Without an explicit UID, the JVM computes one from the class structure, so any change produces a new UID and old data is rejected.

questions.scenario: A partner suggests sending payment instructions to your API as Java-serialised objects 'because it's faster'.
questions.question: What should you answer?
options: Decline: deserialising untrusted bytes can lead to remote code execution; use JSON (or Protobuf) with validation instead
Accept if the payload is compressed
questions.explanation: Deserialisation gadget chains are a well-known attack class. Across trust boundaries use data formats that don't execute code paths on read, and validate input.

questions.scenario: Given `Path base = Path.of("/data")` and `Path f = Path.of("/data/2026/10/nip.csv")`.
questions.question: What does `base.relativize(f)` return?
questions.explanation: relativize builds the relative path from base to f. resolve does the opposite: base.resolve("2026/10/nip.csv") gives f.
